To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD133 and CD56 are correlated in NSCLC and that high CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) infiltration is an independent prognostic indicator in patients with NSCLC.
there is an inverse correlation between the cancer stem cells markers CD133 and CD56, and the immune cell markers CD8 and Hla class I.
there is a negative correlation of CD56 and CD133, which may confirm the possibility of natural killer cells to target cancer stem cell markers in non-small cell carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between cancer stem cells/cell initiating cells and tumor infiltrating lymphocytes.
the correlation of cancer cells and tumor-inflitrating immune cells.
the relationship between cancer stem cell markers (CD133, OCT-4) and immune cell markers (CD8, CD56).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, high HLA class I, low CD133 expression, high CD56 expression, and low PD-L1 expression may predict a good clinical outcome for NSCLC patients.
CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells are the main tumor infiltrating immune cells in non-small-cell lung cancer.
CD133+ cancer initiating cells/cancer stem cells may be targeted by natural killer cells and CD8+ T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune microenvironment in NSCLC can be influenced by cancer stem cells/caner initiating cells.
CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells are associated with a favorable prognosis, whereas cancer stem cell markers are associated with a poor prognosis.
CD56+ natural killer cells may be an important immune cell to target cancer stem cells/caner initiating cells in NSCLL, and CD8+ T cells may be an effective immune cell to target tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD56 expression is a potential biomarker for cancer stem cells/caner initiating cells and CD8 expression is a potential prognostic biomarker for immunotherapy in NSCLC.
the immune microenvironment of NSCLC is complex.
CD8+ T cells may be a potential biomarker of immunotherapy response in NSCLC, which may be used to select patients for treatment.
